title: Valuation ring as the filtered colimit of centre local rings
statement: Let $T$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] over $\mathbf Z$, let $L$ be a separable closure of $k(T)$, and let $V\subseteq L$ be a valuation ring with fraction field $L$ and a prescribed morphism $\operatorname{Spec}V\to T$ restricting to the specified generic map $\operatorname{Spec}L\to T$. Thus $V$ represents a point $x$ of $RZ_L(T)$, the valuation-point space of [lem-trf-riemann-zariski-finite-refinement]. An $L$-quasi-model is an integral scheme $U$ with a separated finite-type map $U\to T$ and a specified dominant generic map $\operatorname{Spec}L\to U$ factoring the generic map to $T$. A centred quasi-model additionally has a lift $\operatorname{Spec}V\to U$ respecting that specified generic map. A refinement from a centred quasi-model $U'$ to $U$ is a $T$-morphism $U'\to U$ respecting the two maps from $\operatorname{Spec}V$ and $\operatorname{Spec}L$. Choose one representative of each isomorphism class of centred quasi-models, ordered by refinement, and write $c_U\in U$ for the image of the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}V$. This is a small directed system; refinement induces an injective local homomorphism $\mathcal O_{U,c_U}\to\mathcal O_{U',c_{U'}}$ inside $L$. The local maps to $V$ identify $V$ with the filtered colimit $\varinjlim_U\mathcal O_{U,c_U}$, and identify $\operatorname{Spec}V$ with the inverse limit of the affine schemes $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{U,c_U}$ with these transition morphisms. These assertions remain valid after restricting to refinements of any fixed centred quasi-model, or to affine centred quasi-models mapping to a fixed affine open neighbourhood of its centre.
